lines.quote: Developed and maintained beamforming algorithms for a 64-element L-band phased-array receiver used in an EORA ocean-monitoring scatterometer.
Implemented the digital beamformer in C++ running on a Xilinx Zynq SoC, meeting real-time throughput requirements for on-board processing at 1.2 Gsamples/s aggregate.

Built and maintained the team's Python-based simulation and test-automation framework (pytest, CI/CD pipeline, ~15k LOC), used by six engineers for regression testing of beamformer firmware against reference models.
Conducted RF characterisation and calibration of array front-end modules using Rohde & Schwarz ZVA network analysers and FSW spectrum analysers in the company's anechoic chamber facility.
Rheinmark Technical University Aachen, Germany — Diplom-Ingenieur, 2004
My Diplom-Ingenieur from Rheinmark TU Aachen was in Electrical Engineering
Implemented an extended Kalman filter for real-time platform attitude estimation, used to compensate antenna pointing errors on airborne radar testbed flights for a GALR contract.
Led a team of four signal processing engineers through the engineering model development and qualification of the digital beamforming subsystem for an EORA Earth observation mission.

Co-authored three peer-reviewed conference papers (SESE Radar Conference 2016, BaRC 2018, IGRSS 2022) on phased-array calibration techniques and adaptive beamforming for spaceborne scatterometers.
Joined as an EU-resident employee on a permanent German contract; transferred to the Finnish office in 2019.
Working language throughout has been English: all design reviews, technical reports, and EORA milestone documentation written and presented in English.
I have been based in Oulu since 2019, when Polaris moved me to their Finnish operations, and I am looking for a permanent position here rather than another contract rotation.
